A chart for planning, not a change to the code. Every entry has a status: decided (by Sam) or recommended (pending Sam). Item 7, the kkt-config breakup in config-split.json, is part of the proposal, accepted by Sam (msg 1979).
rule: Every trait a crate depends on is a contract, and it is declared by its consumers, not by the crate that implements it.

If a contract is used by more than two crates, it lives in its own contract-only crate (traits, pure value types, and test doubles behind `testing`). Its real implementations live in separate implementation crates, which implement it directly (msg 2020); only programs depend on them. Model: kkt-db (contract) and kkt-db-sqlite (implementation).

If it is used by two crates or fewer, each consumer declares its own contract, and the program adapts the implementation to it; the shared assembly crate may write an adapter the programs share (msg 2019).
Used by: crates other than the definer and the implementers that take the trait in a public slot or call through it, in normal dependencies. Test-only use is listed separately.

new_crates.name: kkt-service-os

new_crates.name: kkt-remote-access-os
new_crates.concern: The machine's `tailscale`: `OsHost`, a plain type that implements nothing; the program adapts it to kkt-remote-access's `Host`. kkt-remote-access's `real` feature moves here.

new_crates.name: kkt-client-config-os
new_crates.concern: The machine's files and the `claude` command: `OsHost`, a plain type that implements nothing; the program adapts it to kkt-client-config's `Host`. kkt-client-config's `real` feature moves here.

new_crates.name: kkt-diagnostics-os
new_crates.concern: Key file reads and network probes: `OsProber`, a plain type that implements nothing; the program adapts it to kkt-diagnostics's `Prober`. kkt-diagnostics's `real` feature moves here.

new_crates.name: kkt-lane-files-os
new_crates.concern: The disk and git under a lane folder: `OsDisk`, a plain type that implements nothing; the program adapts it to kkt-lane-files's `Disk`. kkt-lane-files's `real` feature moves here.

new_crates.name: kkt-web-preview
new_crates.concern: The web page's preview over simulated data: `Preview`, which implements the parts of the kkt-api crates the page uses, and `PreviewGate`, which implements kkt-web's `Gate` over kkt-web's sessions, as a program may, with their settings; and the preview example, a dev-only program that serves the page. The preview's tests are here too. Its dev arrows to effect crates (kkt-clock-system, kkt-entropy-os) are the preview example's; the library depends on none.

new_crates.name: kkt-server-listen
new_crates.concern: Binding the server to its socket and serving it: `listen` and `Listening`, which only the programs use. kkt-server's `real` feature moves here. It serves kkt-server's built `App`, so it needs axum.

new_crates.name: kkt-backup-os
new_crates.concern: Writing and pruning backup folders on disk: `write` and `prune`, which the program calls. kkt-backup's `real` feature moves here.

new_crates.name: kkt-shutdown-os
new_crates.concern: The operating system's stop signals: `StopSignals`, which the programs install and which stop kkt-shutdown's `Shutdown`. kkt-shutdown's `real` feature moves here.

new_crates.name: kkt-search
new_crates.concern: Search as text: the words of a text (FTS5 `unicode61`'s rule, with its word table), a search's terms, whether a text matches them, and an excerpt around the matches, drawn with the marks and window it is given; and `Word`. Pure text: it knows no database. kkt-db-sqlite and kkt-db's in-memory backend (behind `testing`) use it. kkt-db-sqlite's test that regenerates the word table writes to its path here, not kkt-db's search/table.rs (tests.rs:346).

new_crates.name: kkt-api-agent
new_crates.concern: What any registered agent may do, and the records every level shares: the agent's operations by area (Api, Agents, Channels, Messages, Memory, Lanes), the records, queries and errors they and the other levels use, Settings and MAX_LANE_DESCRIPTION_CHARS. One of three contract crates, one per level of authority; kkt-api-operator and kkt-api-admin depend on it for the shared records. kkt-rules implements it; /mcp uses only it.

new_crates.name: kkt-api-admin
new_crates.concern: What /mcp-admin's administrator does: the 12 admin_* reads (Admin), and what is server-wide, creating a swarm (Swarms), with AdminChannel. kkt-rules implements it; kkt-mcp, for /mcp-admin, and kkt-mcp-formatter use it, and the fake product creates its second swarm through it.

new_crates.name: kkt-api-operator
new_crates.concern: What the human who runs the server may do: the web page's operator powers, by area (Views, Changes, Lanes, Server), with the records only they use (ChannelActivity, StaleAgent, StaleHidden, Kept, KeptReason, ServerRunInfo, LaneSave, ChannelChange). It depends on kkt-api-agent for the shared records. kkt-rules implements it; the web page and the operator operations /mcp-admin calls use it. Open question: lanes, the server announcement and server runs are server-wide, yet its Lanes and Server traits let a swarm's operator change them; where several swarms each have an operator, changing them may belong in kkt-api-admin, with reading staying here.

new_crates.name: kkt-config-file
new_crates.concern: The config file: reading it (behind `real`) and parsing its TOML into the settings it gives (`parse_file`), and writing a change to its text (`with_allowed_host`). The program adapts it to kkt-settings' source of settings, and to kkt-container's parser for the container's config.

Its test-only implementations, in kkt-mcp's and kkt-identity's tests (and kkt-rules' own), stay as test doubles.

kkt-admission::server_keys::KeyTexts.result: Already rule-shaped: declared by kkt-admission's key check, implemented by each program.

kkt-container::LoginLink.result: Already rule-shaped: declared by kkt-container, implemented by the program.

kkt-remote-access::Host.result: Declared by its consumer, kkt-remote-access. OsHost moves to kkt-remote-access-os as a plain type that implements nothing; kkt-remote-access's real feature moves with it, and the program adapts it.

kkt-diagnostics::Prober.result: Declared by its consumer, kkt-diagnostics. OsProber moves to kkt-diagnostics-os as a plain type that implements nothing; kkt-diagnostics's real feature moves with it, and the program adapts it.

kkt-setup::Ask.result: Already rule-shaped: declared by kkt-setup, implemented by the program.

decided_items.text: random_chars moves to kkt-entropy and takes the alphabet as an argument. ALPHABET becomes private to kkt-rules, for both making and spotting tokens. kkt-admission and kkt-names pass their own character sets. random_chars(alphabet, len) is a provided method of the Entropy trait, written in terms of below, so kkt-entropy is a plain contract crate (msg 2011).

Operator and admin names stay in kkt-names. AdminName is split: its name rules stay in kkt-names; bound_to and bound_in (tying the name to the key's hash) move to kkt-admission. kkt-store's private OPERATOR copy goes, and kkt-store takes it from kkt-names. (kkt-store merged into kkt-rules, msg 2017.)

The history from before kkt-db moves out of the program. kkt-store owned it (kkt-rules since msg 2017) as database-neutral facts (old 21 → core 1, 22 → core 2, the dropped handoff_note columns). kkt-db defines the neutral shape (today kkt-db-sqlite's Legacy). kkt-db-sqlite keeps only the SQLite part (user_version, the adoption). The program wires it and supplies the "upgrade with kkt 0.10 first" message.

kkt-store's testing offers an in-memory store on kkt-db's testing::MemoryPlace, and the fail-a-write hook; since msg 2017 they are kkt-rules' testing::memory and testing::fail_next_write. The tests of kkt-identity-keymode, kkt-mcp, kkt-server and the fake product dev-depend on kkt-rules for them, not on kkt-db or kkt-db-sqlite. kkt-rules' own tests run on both backends.

kkt-agent-client stops depending on kkt-watch. It offers plain methods with its own types (channels, handle, latest ID, message, wait, the admin polling included). The program holds a thin adapter implementing kkt-watch's Server and mapping the failures.
Both Failure enums stay; the program's adapter maps one to the other.

kkt-config is broken up by domain, as proposed (accepted in msg 1979): format and fixed facts move into the crate that owns them, tuning values become settings fields the program fills, operator settings and defaults go to kkt-settings or the program, and kkt-config keeps only what is truly cross-domain. The table lists every item.
Under each type, the page lists the contracts it implements with their methods, then its own methods, in both the current and the proposed map.

The strict rule covers only another crate's contract. A crate may implement its own traits: FixedClock implements Clock, the entropy test doubles implement Entropy, kkt-db's own implementations and MemoryPlace's Evolve stay, DryRun implements System, and SameSource stays in kkt-web and implements Sources (msg 1984). (Since msg 2031, SameSource is gone with Sources.)

(Changed by msgs 2032 and 2042.) kkt-server's Parts took a store; since msg 2042 they take the Rules that kkt-rules' start built, as kkt-api-agent's Api, and kkt-server names no kkt-rules type but OperatorWording, which its Wording implements. The fake product's Product::start keeps kkt-rules' Db, to call start.
(Superseded by the adapter reshape, msg 2009.) Each program wired the Parts slots sources, gate and wording from its adapters; kkt-server now adapts all three itself (A6).
kkt-web's must-not: it depends on no rules, store, admission, identity or implementation crate; kkt-server and the preview implement its contract.
The preview example and the preview's tests move to kkt-web-preview, which has its own assembly. kkt-web's dev arrows to implementation crates go.

(Superseded by the adapter reshape, msg 2009.) Parts took a SourcesFactory and a GateFactory so the programs could adapt what kkt-server builds. With kkt-server adapting them itself (A6), neither is needed.

(Superseded by msgs 2017 and 2020.) Shared adapters lived once, in a composition crate: kkt-store-rules and kkt-db-sqlite-db. kkt-store merged into kkt-rules, and kkt-db-sqlite implements kkt-db's shared contract directly, so neither crate remains.

kkt-format is dissolved (msg 1986). Formatter and what goes with it become kkt-mcp-formatter, in Surfaces, kind logic. NoticeWording moves to kkt-names and takes plain input; kkt-rules still declares OperatorWording, and kkt-server's Wording adapts it.

Layers say where in the system a crate sits, in both maps: Programs, Assembly, Surfaces, Access, Core, Data, Operations, Clients, Foundations and Dev-only. Each implementation crate sits beside its domain; the shared adapter crates sit in Data (msg 1986).

Each crate has a kind, written by hand: contract, logic, effect, composition, configuration or test support, and in the current map mixed. Boxes are outlined in their kind's colour. The generator checks what it can and reports mismatches; in the proposed map a mixed crate is a violation (msg 1981).

No crate in the proposed map is mixed, compositions included (msg 1992): kkt-server's listen and Listening go to kkt-server-listen, kkt-backup's write and prune to kkt-backup-os, and kkt-shutdown's StopSignals to kkt-shutdown-os. Only the programs use them. LogPolicy is configuration: it goes to kkt-settings, so kkt-provenance records it without depending on kkt-logs (msg 1995). Tagged "follows from Sam's rule"; C7 is decided: kkt-server-listen may use axum (msg 2010).

random_chars(alphabet, len) becomes a provided method of Entropy in kkt-entropy, written in terms of below (msg 2011). Its callers, kkt-names, kkt-rules, kkt-admission and kkt-web-preview, use it through Entropy.

Database's thread pool (spawn_blocking in Database::run) moves into kkt-db-sqlite. Backend's read and write become async, so kkt-db no longer needs tokio (msg 2012). Shown on Backend's and Database's docs and on both crates' third-party lists.

kkt-db is contract-only, with no logic crate beside it (msg 2014, replacing msg 2012's). Database disappears: its typed read and write become BackendExt's provided methods, over Backend's async read and write, with a blanket implementation that works through dyn Backend; its fault hook becomes testing::FaultyBackend, a backend that wraps another. migrate and pending become provided methods of Evolve, schema and schema_at Schema's latest and at, and the query checks Schema's check_ methods and operand_type; Step::apply_to stays. Search's text functions, Word and Excerpt move to a new crate, kkt-search (logic, A9, A10); Search and Hit stay in kkt-db.

kkt-store merges into kkt-rules (msg 2017): its queries, its decisions, the core's tables and their history, and item 4's testing helpers. kkt-rules uses kkt-db directly. Reads, Writes and the copied record types go; the database stays private to kkt-rules (msg 2032). Q1 is resolved. CLAUDE.md's rule on where database access lives changes with the code refactor, not in #409.

kkt-server implements kkt-web's Sources and Gate, and adapts the wording, as the adapter the three programs share: "the program adapts", written once in the shared assembly crate, on condition that kkt-server makes no decisions (msg 2019). The page's limits come in at construction (PageLimits), save_lane splits into create_lane and update_lane, and kkt-web works out the operator flag itself (A11). A6 is withdrawn. Changed by msg 2031: kkt-web calls kkt-api-agent directly, so of these only the Gate and the wording remain kkt-server's adapters.

Implementing a shared contract crate's contract is fine, just like consuming it; the strict rule covers only contracts a consumer declares for itself (msg 2020). kkt-db-sqlite implements kkt-db's Backend, Connection and Evolve, the system clock Clock, and OsEntropy Entropy, directly; kkt-db-sqlite-db goes. KeyMode, kkt-agent-client's Remote and AdminRemote, and the six -os crates keep the programs' adapters, with no shared machine contract.

Web sessions move into kkt-web (msg 2021): Sessions (IDs, hashing, expiry, sign-out, form tokens) with clock and entropy injected. The code moves as it is, except that a session holds the gate's own value instead of kkt_admission::Principal, which kkt-web cannot name (kkt-review-373, msg 2030). kkt-admission keeps the access decision. Gate shrinks to admits and sign_in, the two questions for kkt-admission. PreviewGate uses kkt-web's sessions instead of its own copy.

A7 is decided (msg 2022): kkt-web-preview counts as a program. A8 is replaced (msg 2025): kkt-server declares its own WebIdentify for its web gate, kkt-mcp keeps its Identify, and the program adapts the same KeyMode to each.

A1 and A2 are accepted, A3 is changed and A4 and A5 are moot (msg 2027). A crate counts as a user of a contract only if its code calls the contract's methods; naming a trait to wire an implementation in, or to implement it in an adapter, is not use. No contract crosses the line of more than two users either way.

kkt-rules' operations become a shared contract crate, kkt-api (contract, Core), the heart of the application, which web and MCP are today's protocols over (msg 2031). Its traits by area (A13): Api 3, Agents 6, Channels 12, Messages 6, Memory 4, Lanes 11, Server 4 and Operator 10 methods, 56 in all; Admin's 12 are in kkt-api-admin (msg 2042), with the records, queries and errors they use. kkt-rules implements it; kkt-mcp, kkt-mcp-formatter, kkt-web and kkt-identity-keymode use it and depend on no kkt-rules type. kkt-web's copied records, Source, Sources and SameSource go, and kkt-server's RulesSource and RulesSources. The preview implements the parts of kkt-api the page uses. The msg 2019 reshapes land in kkt-api: Api::limits, Lanes' create_lane and update_lane, and the operator flag in its records (A11). CLAUDE.md's kkt-rules, kkt-web and kkt-mcp rows change with the refactor, not in #409. (kkt-api split by level in msg 2045.)

Option (b) for the store (msg 2032): the database stays private to kkt-rules. Recording a run is kkt-rules' start, which builds the Rules (msg 2042). tests/migrations/v0_10_0.rs moves into kkt-rules' tests; other crates' test setup goes through kkt-api, or a kkt-rules helper behind testing. A12 is withdrawn. (kkt-api split by level in msg 2045.)

Msg 2042: kkt-rules' start records the run and builds the Rules, which the programs pass into kkt-server's Parts; record_run leaves kkt-api. A9, A10 and A11 are accepted. The Admin trait (12 admin_* reads) and AdminChannel move to their own contract crate, kkt-api-admin, which kkt-rules implements and only the crates that serve admin use. The Operator trait's side is on hold, as is the fake product's second swarm. (kkt-api split by level in msg 2045.)

Msg 2045, replacing msg 2042's item 3: kkt-api splits into three contract crates, one per level of authority, and there is no plain kkt-api. kkt-api-agent: Api 3, Agents 6, Channels 12, Messages 6, Memory 4, Lanes 3 (34), with the shared records. kkt-api-operator: Views 5, Changes 6, Lanes 8, Server 3 (22), with its own records. kkt-api-admin: Admin 12 and Swarms 1 (13), with AdminChannel. kkt-rules implements all three. /mcp uses only kkt-api-agent; the page uses agent and operator; /mcp-admin uses admin and the operator operations it calls, so kkt-mcp depends on all three. Creating a swarm is kkt-api-admin's, which the fake product calls. Q2 is resolved: no shared adapter crates. Where the sorting was uncertain is listed in A13.

Msg 2052: A13's sortings are accepted, except that lanes, the server announcement and server runs stay operator-level only for now, to revisit (Q7). The default name pack moves to kkt-settings (DEFAULT_NAME_PACK), so kkt-container no longer depends on kkt-api-agent. The rules slot, one value meeting every trait kkt-server hands on, stands.

Msg 2111: the configuration kind goes, since it named a domain, not what a crate does. kkt-config goes: WEB_SESSION_ID_CHARS to kkt-web, check_access_key, MIN_ACCESS_KEY_BYTES and ACCESS_KEY_FILE_MODE to kkt-admission (kkt-backup, kkt-client-config and kkt-container state their own private-file modes), and InvalidSetting to kkt-settings. kkt-settings is logic and declares SettingsSource; a new effect crate, kkt-config-file, reads and parses the config file, and the program adapts it and the flags to that source. kkt-container parses the container's config through its own ConfigReader, which the program adapts kkt-config-file to.

not_traits.note: Concrete types, not traits, so the rule does not apply as written. Shutdown is taken by kkt-server's build and kkt-mcp's transport; StopSignals, the real signals behind `real`, is used only by programs.

conflicts.title: Real implementations behind `real`, or in implementation crates
conflicts.text: PRINCIPLES rule 8 and CLAUDE.md put what touches the machine in the crate that owns the area, behind its `real` feature, and the rule moves it to implementation crates.
conflicts.resolution: Resolved by the strict rule (decided by Sam): each OS implementation moves to its own `*-os` crate as a plain type that implements nothing, and the consumer's `real` feature moves with it. The program writes one adapter per consumer trait: Host for kkt-container, kkt-remote-access and kkt-client-config, System, Prober and Disk.

conflicts.title: Reads and Writes: the store's contract, or the rules'
conflicts.text: Reads and Writes have one consumer, kkt-rules, so the rule has kkt-rules declare them. The plan has a second store (kkt-pro's) used through the same Reads and Writes, with the agreement test and the two-swarm test over those traits.
conflicts.resolution: Decided by Sam (msg 2017): kkt-store merges into kkt-rules. Its queries, its decisions (the swarm checks, lane version numbering, ChannelScope's translation), the core's tables and their history move into kkt-rules, which uses kkt-db directly as a consumer of a shared contract crate. Reads, Writes, the 36 copied record types, kkt-store and kkt-store-rules all go, with no adapter. Since msg 2015 showed that kkt-store decides things, A6 does not cover it. CLAUDE.md's rule that kkt-rules reaches the database only through Reads and Writes, and its kkt-store row, change with the code refactor, not in this chart.

conflicts.title: kkt-server's web adapters
conflicts.text: Step 6 made kkt-server's adapters to kkt-web's contract public, for a product that builds its own page; the rule would have the programs adapt them.
conflicts.resolution: Decided by Sam (msg 2031, changing msg 2019): kkt-web calls the kkt-api crates directly, so RulesSource and RulesSources go and the page's data needs no adapter. kkt-web's contract keeps only what is web-specific: the Gate, which kkt-server's AdmissionGate implements once for the three programs, deciding nothing (msg 2019), over kkt-web's own sessions (msg 2021). The msg 2019 reshapes land in kkt-api-agent: the limits the rules enforce in Api::limits, create_lane and update_lane in Lanes, and the operator flag in its records (A11).

conflicts.title: Who adapts OperatorWording
conflicts.text: The rule says the program adapts; kkt-format's NoticeWording is wired into the rules by kkt-server, which is not a program.
conflicts.resolution: Decided by Sam (msg 2019): as C4. kkt-server's Wording adapts kkt-names' NoticeWording to OperatorWording once, for the three programs, and hands it to the rules.

conflicts.title: The model's own traits fall below the threshold
conflicts.text: Counted by the rule, kkt-db's Backend and Evolve have no consumer besides kkt-db itself, and Connection one, so they would not get a contract crate.
conflicts.resolution: Decided by Sam (msg 2020): implementing a shared contract crate's contract is fine, just like consuming it. kkt-db is one, so kkt-db-sqlite's SqlitePlace implements Backend, Connection and Evolve directly, and kkt-db-sqlite-db and its 14-method adapter are gone.

conflicts.title: axum outside the three crates CLAUDE.md allows
conflicts.text: CLAUDE.md: axum is the HTTP framework of kkt-web, kkt-mcp and kkt-server only, and its types do not leave those three. kkt-server-listen serves the App kkt-server builds, which holds an axum Router, so it needs axum and the Router.
conflicts.resolution: Decided by Sam (msg 2010): kkt-server-listen may use axum. CLAUDE.md will name it beside kkt-web, kkt-mcp and kkt-server with the code refactor, not in this chart.

withdrawn.text: Identify (one identity decision, or one per consumer) is not a conflict (Sam, via sage-cardinal, msg 1939): a shared trait does not guarantee one decision; the wiring does. kkt-server takes one identify value, which meets both consumer-declared traits, and gives that same value to /mcp, /mcp-admin and the web gate; the program wires KeyMode once. Since msg 2025, kkt-mcp and kkt-server each declare their own (Identify, and WebIdentify for the web gate), and the program wires the same KeyMode into both.

Withdrawn entirely (msg 2019). It said an adapter that decides nothing is a composition. For kkt-store it failed, since kkt-store decides things (msg 2015), and kkt-store merged into kkt-rules (msg 2017). For kkt-server Sam ruled directly: implementing kkt-web's Sources and Gate is "the program adapts", written once in the assembly crate the three programs share, on condition that kkt-server makes no decisions.

Withdrawn (msg 2032): Sam chose option (b). The database stays private to kkt-rules; record_run is an operation in kkt-api, the 0.10.0 migration test moves into kkt-rules' tests, and other crates' test setup goes through kkt-api or a kkt-rules helper behind testing.

assumptions.text: Accepted by Sam (msg 2027): SeededEntropy (repeatable randomness for the web preview and the fake product's differential test, never for tokens) counts as a test double, so it moves into kkt-entropy behind `testing`, not to an implementation crate.

Accepted by Sam (msg 2027): kkt-service's DryRun wraps another System and only prints what it would do; it is the crate's own logic over its contract, not a real implementation, so it stays. It records changes in a list and passes reads through, with no effects of its own.

Changed by Sam (msg 2027): a crate or program counts as a user (consumer) of a contract only if its code calls the contract's methods. Naming a trait to wire an implementation in (for example Box<dyn watch::Server>, to pick Remote or AdminRemote), or to implement it in an adapter, is not use. Recounted from the code: the trait table lists, for each contract, the crates that only wire it in. No contract crosses the line of more than two users either way. Clock goes from 14 users to 13 (kkt-server only wires it). Entropy goes from 5 to 3 (kkt-server and the fake product only wire it), and to 5 in the proposal, so it stays a shared contract. kkt-watch's Server goes from 1 user beyond its declarer to 0 (the program only picks one): kkt-watch itself, which calls it in watch::run, is its one user, so it still declares it. kkt-admission keeps Entropy: SharedKey::generate draws new access keys with it (shared_key.rs:38), besides the session IDs that move to kkt-web.

Moot (msg 2027). (Moot since msg 2017: with kkt-store merged into kkt-rules there are no copies.) "The record types Reads and Writes use" was taken as the 36 public types of kkt-store that the two traits' methods name (32), or that appear inside those types (AgentLaneRecord, ChannelNoteRecord, LaneSourceRecord) or inside StoreResult (StoreError).
Moot (msg 2027). (Moot since msg 2017.) kkt-rules no longer named kkt-store's Db: its Deps and CommandLine took a store meeting its Reads and Writes. Now Deps and CommandLine take kkt-rules' own Db.

Decided by Sam (msg 2022): kkt-web-preview counts as a program, like kkt-fake-product: a dev-only package whose library exists for its own example and tests. So its Preview implements the parts of the kkt-api crates the page uses (msg 2031), and its PreviewGate implements kkt-web's Gate over kkt-web's sessions (msg 2021).

Replaced by Sam's ruling (msg 2025): kkt-server declares its own one-method contract for its web gate, WebIdentify (which operator is this principal, in which swarm), and kkt-mcp keeps its own Identify. The program wires the same KeyMode into both, adapting it to each (3 and 1 methods). No shared trait and no exception. (Msg 2022's description was based on a stale checkout: kkt-server's AdmissionGate does ask the identity, kkt-review-373, msg 2024.)

Accepted by Sam (msg 2042): kkt-search sits in Foundations: it is pure text that the data crates build on and knows nothing of them, as kkt-clock and kkt-entropy sit under the crates that use them (msg 2014 left the layer to us).

Accepted by Sam (msg 2042): Excerpt stays in kkt-db as a plain value: it is part of what a caller asks for in a Search, and msg 2014 has kkt-store's code (now kkt-rules') use only Search and Hit. kkt-search's excerpt takes the marks and window as arguments, so kkt-db needs kkt-search only under `testing`, for its in-memory backend, and kkt-rules does not name kkt-search. Recommended by kkt-review-373 (msg 2018); msg 2014 listed Excerpt among what moves, so this is for Sam.

Accepted by Sam (msg 2042): Whether a message's author, or a channel's last speaker, is the operator is part of the kkt-api records (kkt-api-agent's Message, kkt-api-operator's ChannelActivity), filled by kkt-rules, which makes the operator an actor and names it. With kkt-web rendering kkt-api-agent's records directly (msg 2031), the flag belongs with the record, not with each surface. kkt-web's live notices, which come from kkt-events, still work it out with kkt-names' is_operator.

Decided by Sam (msgs 2045 and 2052): the operations are split by who may call them, into kkt-api-agent (34), kkt-api-operator (22) and kkt-api-admin (13), each split by area. Rule used: an operation that takes an &Agent is the agent level's; one that takes an &Operator is the operator level's, or the admin's for the admin_* reads; one that takes an Actor goes by who calls it today. The ones I was unsure of, for Sam: (1) set_purpose takes an Actor; agents (channel owners) and the operator both call it, so it sits with the agent level and the operator calls it with its own authority. (2) register_with_client and reclaim_with_client are called before the caller is a registered agent; they sit with the agent level as its entry points. (3) current_server_announcement is read by every agent and by /mcp-admin; agent level. (4) subscribe is called only by the page, and hears every notice in the swarm, closed channels included; operator level. (5) Lanes, the announcement and server runs are server-wide (CLAUDE.md), which could make their changes admin; the web page's operator changes them today, so they are the operator level's, as msg 2045's examples have them. (6) save_lane, lane and lanes_page are called only by /mcp-admin, under the operator's Read and Change permissions; operator level, which /mcp-admin uses. (7) stale_agents, hide_stale_agents, hide_agent, change_channel and create_channel_as_operator are called by both the page and /mcp-admin; operator level. (8) in_swarm and limits are needed at every level; they sit in the agent level's Api, which the others depend on. (9) The shared records are in kkt-api-agent, AgentView included, since both operator (agent_view) and admin (admin_agent) return it; only ChannelActivity, StaleAgent, StaleHidden, Kept, KeptReason, ServerRunInfo, LaneSave and ChannelChange are operator-only, and AdminChannel admin-only. Sam accepted cases 1 to 4 and 6 to 9 as reasoned (msg 2052). Case 5 stays operator-level for now, to revisit (Q7).

Decided (msgs 2042 and 2045): kkt-rules' start records the run, then builds and returns the Rules; the programs call it and pass the Rules into kkt-server's Parts. record_run is not an API operation, since the run_id goes into the Deps that build the Rules (kkt-review-373, msg 2036). Creating a swarm is kkt-api-admin's Swarms::create_swarm, which the fake product calls.

doc_edits.doc: The server over the admin endpoint, `/mcp-admin`, for `kkt watch --admin`: every channel, closed and hidden ones included, through plain methods; the program adapts it to kkt-watch's `Server`.

How notices name the operator, from the admin key's name or none: "The operator", or "The operator (via <name>)". It takes plain input, so kkt-names knows nothing of kkt-rules' Audit; the program's adapter maps Audit to it and meets kkt-rules' OperatorWording.
A database a store can run work on, through BackendExt. `read` and `write` are async: a backend that blocks, as SQLite does, runs the work on a thread pool of its own.
Who is viewing: whether a key lets a viewer in (sign_in), and who a signed-in or open viewer is (admits). kkt-web keeps the sessions itself.
Admission for the web page: whether sign-in is needed, whether a key is good and whom it admits, and the decision for an open page. The sessions are kkt-web's.
For other crates' tests: Rules over an in-memory database, the fail-a-write hook, and the check that two swarms stay apart.
Checks that two swarms stay apart in a database that holds no avatars or channels yet: a swarm sees and changes nothing of another.
The core's database, private to kkt-rules but for opening it: the program gives Db::new a kkt-db backend.
The parts the server is built from: the clock and entropy, the identity for the endpoints and for the web gate, and the Rules, as one value meeting the kkt-api contracts it hands on.

status_legend: "Decided by Sam" covers the rule itself (msg 1938) and what follows from it, and Sam's rulings: msgs 1939 and 1952, the strict rule (msg 1978), and item 7, the kkt-config breakup, accepted as proposed (msg 1979); msg 1984's fixes and its items 7 and 8 (accepted in msg 1987); and the layers, kinds and kkt-format's dissolving (msgs 1981 and 1986). "Recommended, pending Sam" is what rests on an assumption, which leaves nothing pending; Q7 is a decision Sam will revisit (msg 2052). "Follows from Sam's rule" marks what the rule requires once its checks run, without a ruling of its own (msg 1992): the effects split out of kkt-server, kkt-backup and kkt-shutdown.

strict.text: No implementation implements a contract that another crate declares for itself; the program adapts (Sam, msg 1978). Implementing a shared contract crate's contract is fine, just like consuming it: the strict rule covers only consumer-declared contracts (msg 2020). The shared assembly crate kkt-server writes the adapters the three programs share, as the program would, on condition that it decides nothing (msg 2019). A crate may implement its own traits: FixedClock implements Clock, the entropy test doubles implement Entropy, kkt-db's own implementations and MemoryPlace's Evolve stay, and DryRun implements System (msg 1984; SameSource went with Sources in msg 2031). Sam rejected the refinement of msg 1952, which let an implementation implement its one consumer's contract directly, because it leads to tight coupling.

renames.concern: Key mode's identity: `KeyMode`, a plain type that implements nothing; it decides who a caller is from the key that let it in and the avatar's token, and kkt and kkt-keymode adapt it to kkt-mcp's `Identify` and kkt-server's `WebIdentify`.

The MCP tools' results turned into text or JSON, within the response size cap: `Formatter`, `Format`, its `Settings` and `MIN_RESPONSE_BYTES`. It is what was left of kkt-format, which is dissolved; `NoticeWording` moved to kkt-names.

kkt-clock.concern: Time: the `Clock` contract, kkt's time types `Time` and `Span`, the time text functions, and `FixedClock` behind `testing`. Contract-only: its real clock is in kkt-clock-system. The only crate that uses chrono.

kkt-names.concern: Avatars' handles, channel IDs, the name packs, and the operator and admin names with their rules. It draws randomness through kkt-entropy's `Entropy`, with its own character sets.

kkt-rules.concern: Every permission decision and every change, for agents and the operator, each in one swarm: Rules implements the application's shared contracts, kkt-api-agent, kkt-api-operator and kkt-api-admin. It holds the core's data privately: its queries as kkt-db operations on a Db it is given, the core's tables as migrations with their history from before kkt-db, and the check that swarms stay apart. kkt-store merged into it; the database stays private.
kkt-rules.must_not: Name a database or use a database library: it reaches the database through kkt-db's contract, which the program fills with the SQLite backend.

kkt-db-sqlite.concern: SQLite, the only crate that knows it: it opens a SQLite database, in a file or in memory, adopts a database from before kkt-db by SQLite's `user_version`, and copies one for backups. SqlitePlace implements kkt-db's Backend, Connection and Evolve directly, since kkt-db is a shared contract crate, and runs the blocking work on tokio's blocking pool.

kkt-db.concern: The database contract, for any database: values, tables, keys and constraints; a narrow language of questions and changes (not SQL), with Schema's checks of which are valid; transactions, through Backend and the typed read and write BackendExt provides; search's Search and Hit; migrations as additions, run by Evolve's provided migrate and pending; the shape of a database from before kkt-db; and its own in-memory backend and fault-injecting backend behind `testing`. Every behaviour is a method of its own traits and types. kkt-db-sqlite implements it directly, as a shared contract.

kkt-server.concern: Assembling the server from its parts and running it: the rules, `/mcp`, `/mcp-admin` and the web page. Its parts take the Rules that kkt-rules' `start` built, as one value meeting every kkt-api contract it hands on, and the identity twice: meeting kkt-mcp's `Identify`, which it hands to the endpoints, and its own `WebIdentify`, which its web gate asks. It writes the adapters the three programs share, once, and decides nothing: AdmissionGate implements kkt-web's Gate, and Wording adapts kkt-names' NoticeWording to kkt-rules' OperatorWording. It builds the page's sessions and page-only limits. Binding the socket is in kkt-server-listen.

kkt-agent-client.concern: The shared MCP client for agent commands: avatar credentials, and reaching the server as an agent or admin through plain methods with its own types. It knows nothing of kkt-watch; the program adapts it.

kkt-mcp.concern: The agent and admin MCP tools, what the two share, their HTTP transport, and what agents are told about each tool. It calls the kkt-api crates directly and depends on no kkt-rules type: kkt-api-agent for /mcp, and for /mcp-admin kkt-api-admin and the operator operations it offers. It declares the `Identify` it asks; kkt-server hands it the program's adapter.

kashkeshet.concern: The `kkt` command and everything it does on a machine: its subcommands and the files and environment they read, the settings and config file, the setup record, key files, how a client reaches the server, and one module per command that takes plain inputs. It holds the adapters the strict rule needs: one per consumer-declared contract it fills with another crate's implementation (KeyMode, kkt-agent-client's watching, and the six -os crates). Shared contracts' implementations need none, and kkt-server writes the web page's and the wording's adapters for it.

kkt-keymode.concern: A second program that assembles key mode again from the shared crates with none of the `kkt` program's code, with its own adapters, as the strict rule has every program write, and the shared store and database adapters. The HTTP-only end-to-end tests run against it in CI. Dev-only, never released.

kkt-fake-product.concern: The shared crates assembled as a product other than kkt would assemble them, with two swarms and `FakeIdentify`, its own type meeting kkt-mcp's `Identify` and kkt-server's `WebIdentify`. It adapts the implementations it wires, as every program does, and takes the shared database adapter. Its tests check that nothing of one swarm reaches the other. Dev-only, never released.

kkt-admission.concern: Whether an HTTP caller is let in at all, and as which `Principal`: no key, which of the server's keys, or (for another program's `Identify` to judge) any bearer token. Also the checks on the server's keys, and which admin name a key carries (`server_keys::bound_to`, `bound_in`). The web page's sessions are kkt-web's; for the page it answers whether sign-in is needed, whether a key is good and whom it admits.

kkt-container.concern: Running kkt in Docker: its Compose files, its folder, and the commands that set it up, start, back up, upgrade and stop it. It declares the `Host` it runs them through; the real one is in kkt-container-os, adapted by the program. It reads the container's config through its Host and parses it through its own ConfigReader.

kkt-service.concern: Running kkt as a service under launchd or systemd, and the plan of what the service runs. It declares the `System` it works through, and keeps `DryRun`; the real one is in kkt-service-os, adapted by the program.

kkt-remote-access.concern: Sharing a service-mode server over the machine's existing Tailscale login. It declares the `Host` it works through; the real one is in kkt-remote-access-os, adapted by the program.

kkt-client-config.concern: MCP client configs and their file formats, so `kkt connect` can add kkt to a client. It declares the `Host` it works through; the real one is in kkt-client-config-os, adapted by the program.

kkt-diagnostics.concern: `kkt doctor`'s checks and their plan, and setup's wait for a new server. It declares the `Prober` it checks through; the real one is in kkt-diagnostics-os, adapted by the program.

kkt-lane-files.concern: Lanes as files: the `<lane>.md` format, reading and writing a folder of them, and the folder's git commit. It declares the `Disk` it works through; the real one is in kkt-lane-files-os, adapted by the program.

kkt-web.concern: The human's pages, over the application's operations: it calls kkt-api-agent and kkt-api-operator directly and renders their records. Its own contract keeps only what is web-specific: `Gate` says whether a key lets a viewer in and who a viewer is. It keeps the sign-in sessions and form tokens itself, the page-only limits (`PageLimits`), and its live updates, which it draws from kkt-api-operator's subscribe. The page scenarios every implementation must pass (`testing`).
kkt-web.must_not: Depend on the rules, the store, admission or identity, or on an implementation crate: it uses the agent and operator levels' contracts, and kkt-server implements its Gate.

kkt-events.concern: Notices of new messages, agents, channels and members, and of hidden agents and channels: one bus for the server, each notice heard only in its swarm, with a buffer per swarm kept only while it has a subscriber. The buffer's size is a setting the program fills.

kkt-watch.concern: `kkt watch`: waiting for an agent's new messages (or every channel's, as admin) and the line printed for each. The server, clock, saved place, output and its retry and wait timings are injected by the program.

kkt-backup.concern: Backup folders: their names, what goes in them and their file modes, and which to prune; the disk work is in kkt-backup-os.

kkt-shutdown.concern: The stop signal: `Shutdown`, whose clones share one signal. The operating system's signals are in kkt-shutdown-os.

kkt-settings.concern: Gathering a server's settings: it combines the sources of settings it declares (`SettingsSource`: the command-line flags, the config file) with explicit defaults, flags over the file over defaults, checks every value, and gives each crate the settings it needs. Also the default paths, and the error every settings check gives (`InvalidSetting`).
kkt-settings.must_not: Read files or the environment: the program adapts the config file and the flags to its sources.

page_rules: Every trait a crate depends on is a contract, declared by the crates that use it, not by the crate that implements it. A crate uses a contract when its code calls the contract's methods; naming a trait only to wire an implementation in, or to implement it, is not use.

A contract used by more than two crates lives in a contract-only crate of its own (traits, plain value types with pure behaviour on them, and test doubles behind `testing`). Any crate may implement a shared contract crate's contract directly. Model: kkt-db (contract) and kkt-db-sqlite (implementation).

A contract used by two crates or fewer is declared by each of them. No implementation implements a contract another crate declares for itself: the program adapts the implementation to it. kkt-server, the assembly the three server programs share, writes the adapters they would each write, once, and decides nothing.
A crate may implement its own traits (FixedClock implements Clock, DryRun implements System).

Each crate is one kind, by what it does: contract, logic, effect, composition or test support. Only programs and compositions depend on effect crates, and no crate mixes logic or a contract with an effect.

The application's operations are three contract crates, one per level of authority: kkt-api-agent (what any registered agent may do, and the shared records), kkt-api-operator (what the human who runs the server may do) and kkt-api-admin (what the administrator does). kkt-rules implements all three.
